correctness.rationale: Relabel p<=q=1-p and set d=log(q/p); the centered law is -pd (probability q) and qd (probability p). All stop-loss a ranges were checked exactly against E(Exp(1)-1-a)_+: a<=-1 gives equality, -1<a<-pd follows log b<=b-1, a>=qd is trivial. In the interior R(a)=p(qd-a)exp(1+a) has its maximum p^p q^q<=1 when d>=1, or pd exp(1-pd)<=1 when d<1. Equal means plus all stop-loss bounds proves convex order. Independent numerical endpoint/critical-threshold checks were consistent; the analytic inequalities, not samples, prove all p and a.
residual_risks: No assertion for larger sample sizes or nonbinary alphabets; the MGF consequence is prior art.

value.rationale: The full convex-order comparison is a natural strong stochastic-order bound for an information statistic; it controls every convex risk/test simultaneously and is strictly more informative than the already-known one-sided gamma MGF.
